name: A1.1.1 System Resource Monitoring Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain monitoring capabilities for critical system resources across all infrastructure components. This includes establishing automated monitoring for CPU utilization, memory consumption, storage capacity, and network bandwidth. Monitoring tools shall be configured to collect metrics at appropriate intervals and retain historical data sufficient for trend analysis. Alert thresholds shall be defined and documented to notify appropriate personnel when resource utilization approaches critical levels.

Implementation: CloudWatch collects Lambda invocation, duration, error, and memory metrics, and CloudWatch alarms fire on the defined thresholds. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, Lambda App Events.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: A1.1.2 Capacity Planning and Forecasting
description:
The organization shall establish a capacity planning process that includes regular review of resource utilization trends and forecasting of future capacity requirements. This process shall consider business growth projections, seasonal variations, and planned system changes. Capacity assessments shall be conducted at least annually, with documented plans for capacity expansion when utilization trends indicate potential resource constraints. The organization shall maintain documented procedures for scaling infrastructure resources to meet anticipated demand.

Implementation: CloudWatch retains metric history for trend analysis and DocumentDB storage growth is tracked in the cluster console. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS DocumentDB Cluster.
notes: Implementation: role; "board meetings" -> management meeting (R2). Decisions applied: D25.

name: A1.1 The entity maintains, monitors, and evaluates current processing capacity and use of system components (infras
description:
A1.1 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity maintains, monitors, and evaluates current processing capacity and use of system components (infrastructure, data, and software) to manage capacity demand and to enable the implementation of additional capacity to help meet its objectives.

Monitor your system resources to ensure you have enough capacity to meet demand. Track CPU, memory, storage, and network usage, forecast future needs based on growth trends, and add capacity before you run out. This prevents slowdowns or outages due to resource exhaustion.

Implementation: CloudWatch monitors Lambda and DocumentDB capacity and alarms fire on threshold breaches. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, Lambda App Events.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: A1.2.1 Cloud Infrastructure Environmental Protection and Redundancy
description:
The organization shall ensure that cloud service providers maintain appropriate environmental protections and redundancy capabilities for hosted infrastructure. This includes verification that cloud providers implement physical security controls, redundant power systems, fire suppression, climate control, and geographic redundancy. Reliance on enterprise cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) satisfies environmental protection requirements, provided proper due diligence is documented.

Implementation: Physical security, redundant power, and environmental controls are provided by AWS data centers and verified through the AWS SOC 2 report reviewed in the AWS vendor assessment in the compliance platform.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; No task linked; the AWS vendor assessment record (Compliance Platform Vendor Assessment) is the evidence.

name: A1.2.2 Data Backup and Recovery Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain comprehensive data backup procedures to ensure business continuity and data protection. This includes automated backup configurations for all critical systems and data, offsite or geographically distributed backup storage, defined retention periods aligned with business requirements, and documented recovery procedures. Backup integrity shall be verified through regular restoration testing to confirm recoverability.

Implementation: DocumentDB automated backups are retained 35 days with point-in-time recovery enabled, and a backup-restore test is run quarterly and recorded in the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, AWS DocumentDB Cluster.
notes: Implementation: r5; 7-day retention -> 35 days (R3/R5, D27); quarterly restore test added (R3).

name: A1.2.3 Disaster Recovery Planning and Testing
description:
The organization shall maintain a disaster recovery plan that addresses alternate processing capabilities and recovery procedures in the event of primary system failure. The plan shall define recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for critical systems, document failover procedures, and identify responsible personnel. The disaster recovery plan shall be tested at least annually to validate effectiveness and updated based on test results and organizational changes.

Implementation: DocumentDB cluster storage is replicated across three availability zones and the single serverless instance is re-created automatically after any failure, including an availability-zone failure; the compliance platform BCP dashboard records an RTO of 2 hours for AWS infrastructure, and the BCP full test executed February 4, 2026 completed with a 100 % success rate. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Cluster, Compliance Platform Bcp Dashboard, Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, r4; "across 3 availability zones" -> storage replicated across three AZs (D26, 2026-11-01; was Multi-AZ per R3); "Q1 2025" test label dropped in favour of the execution date (D18).

name: A1.2 The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains environmen
description:
A1.2 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains environmental protections, backup processes, and recovery infrastructure to meet its objectives.

Protect your systems from environmental threats and ensure you can recover from disasters. This includes physical protections (like fire suppression and backup power), regular data backups stored offsite, and alternate processing capabilities if your primary site fails. Test your backup and recovery procedures regularly.

Implementation: AWS data centers are SOC 2 attested; DocumentDB storage is replicated across three availability zones, with automated backups retained 35 days and point-in-time recovery enabled. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, AWS DocumentDB Cluster.
notes: Implementation: r5; 7-day retention -> 35 days (D27).

name: A1.3.1 Recovery Plan Testing Schedule and Execution
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal schedule for testing recovery plan procedures at least annually. Testing shall include scenarios relevant to distributed operations such as cloud service failover, remote access restoration, and data recovery from backup systems. Tests shall be documented with clear objectives, scope, and success criteria defined prior to execution. All key personnel shall participate in testing exercises appropriate to their roles.

Implementation: The BCP full test (plan: AWS Service Disruption Recovery; scenario: full system recovery from backups using infrastructure as code) was executed February 4, 2026 with the CEO as coordinator. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: role; Coordinator named by role instead of person; "Q1 2025" label dropped (D18).

name: A1.3.2 Recovery Test Results Documentation and Plan Updates
description:
The organization shall formally document the results of all recovery plan tests, including any deficiencies, failures, or areas for improvement identified during testing. Test results shall be reviewed by appropriate personnel, and the recovery plan shall be updated to address identified gaps or lessons learned. A tracking mechanism shall be maintained to ensure all identified issues are remediated and incorporated into updated recovery procedures within a reasonable timeframe.

Implementation: Test results are recorded in the compliance platform BCP test record: status Completed, success rate 100 %, system recovered successfully, plan status Active, one exercise to date. Evidence: Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Implementation: humadroid; "Q1 2025" label dropped (D18).

name: A1.3 The entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives.
description:
A1.3 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives.

Regularly test your ability to recover from various disaster scenarios. Include tests of data restoration, failover to backup systems, and operation from alternate locations. Involve key personnel in tests, document results, and update plans based on what you learn. Testing reveals problems before you face a real disaster.

Implementation: The BCP full test executed February 4, 2026 (full system recovery from backups using infrastructure as code) completed with status Completed and a 100 % success rate. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Implementation: none; "Q1 2025" label dropped (D18).

name: C1.1.1 Confidential Information Classification Policy
description:
Establish and maintain a formal policy that defines what constitutes confidential information within the organization. The policy shall include a classification scheme (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) with clear criteria for each level. The policy should specifically address classification of digital assets, cloud-stored documents, and information shared via collaboration tools. The policy must identify categories of confidential information including but not limited to: trade secrets, financial data, strategic plans, customer information, pricing data, intellectual property, and partner-designated confidential materials. All personnel must acknowledge understanding of the classification policy.

Implementation: The Data Classification and Handling Standard defines four tiers (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) with criteria per tier; personnel acknowledge it in the compliance platform portal.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Tier names taken from the C1.1 note; acknowledgment mechanism per R6/R8.

name: C1.1.2 Confidential Information Identification and Labeling Procedures
description:
Implement procedures for identifying and properly labeling confidential information when created internally or received from external parties. This includes establishing naming conventions and metadata tagging for digital files, configuring document management systems to support classification labels, and defining procedures for marking confidential information in emails and shared documents. Procedures shall address how personnel identify confidential information during creation, receipt, and processing activities. Regular reviews shall be conducted to ensure classification remains appropriate as information ages or business circumstances change.

Implementation: Confidential information is identified by tier using the handling rules in the Data Classification and Handling Standard; data lives in known DocumentDB collections and S3 buckets, with CloudFormation tags on resources.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r4; v1 "metadata tagging" and file labeling removed per R4 (classification metadata/tags row); replaced with the R4 compensating wording.

name: C1.1.3 Confidential Information Retention and Protection Requirements
description:
Define and implement retention requirements and protection controls for confidential information based on business needs, contractual obligations, and legal requirements. Establish technical controls including encryption for data at rest and in transit, access restrictions based on classification level, and secure cloud storage configurations. Implement digital equivalents of clean desk policies for remote workstations. Define retention periods for each classification level and establish legal hold procedures to prevent premature destruction of information needed for litigation or investigations. Assign clear ownership for confidential information management responsibilities.

Implementation: Data at rest is encrypted with KMS customer-managed keys and personnel devices with FileVault; retention periods per tier are set in the Data Retention and Disposal Policy. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys, MacOS FileVault Status.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific.

name: C1.1 The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confid
description:
C1.1 (C1 - Confidentiality Criteria): The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.

Establish a comprehensive program for managing confidential information throughout its lifecycle. Start by defining what constitutes confidential information in your organization - this typically includes trade secrets, financial data, strategic plans, customer lists, pricing information, intellectual property, and any information marked as confidential by partners. Create procedures to identify and properly label confidential information when it's created internally or received from external parties. Implement classification schemes (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) with clear criteria for each level. Define retention requirements for each type of confidential information based on business needs, contractual obligations, and legal requirements. Ensure confidential information is protected from unauthorized access throughout its retention period using appropriate technical controls (encryption, access restrictions) and physical controls (locked storage, clean desk policies). Prevent premature destruction by implementing hold procedures for information needed for litigation or investigations. Regular reviews ensure classification remains appropriate as information ages or circumstances change. Train personnel on recognizing and properly handling confidential information.

Implementation: Data is classified into four tiers (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) under the Data Classification and Handling Standard and encrypted at rest with KMS. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific.

name: C1.2.1 Confidential Information Disposal Policy and Procedures
description:
Establish and maintain a formal policy governing the secure disposal of confidential information. The policy shall define clear triggers for disposal including end of retention periods, project completion, contract termination, and explicit disposal requests. Document appropriate destruction methods based on data sensitivity levels: simple deletion for low-risk data, secure overwriting for moderate risk, and physical destruction or cryptographic erasure for high-risk data. For physical documents, specify cross-cut shredding requirements. Given the remote work environment, include specific guidance for disposal of confidential information on personal devices and home office equipment.

Implementation: Disposal triggers (retention expiry, contract termination, deletion requests) are defined in the Data Retention and Disposal Policy; KMS key deletion provides cryptographic erasure. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Implementation: none; Wording tightened only.

name: C1.2.2 Disposal Execution and Verification Records
description:
Implement a systematic process for executing and documenting the destruction of confidential information across all storage locations. Maintain detailed destruction records including what was destroyed, destruction date, method employed, responsible party, and authorizing authority. For third-party destruction services, obtain and retain certificates of destruction. Verify destruction completeness by confirming removal from all storage locations including primary systems, backups, archives, and remote employee devices. Conduct periodic audits to verify disposal procedures are followed consistently across the organization.

Implementation: Deletions are evidenced by CloudTrail (KMS key usage), S3 access logs, and CloudWatch Logs, and dated disposal entries are recorded in the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups.
notes: Implementation: specific; Dated disposal entry in the compliance platform per R4 (DSR runbook row).

name: C1.2 The entity disposes of confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.
description:
C1.2 (C1 - Confidentiality Criteria): The entity disposes of confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.

Implement secure disposal procedures to ensure confidential information cannot be recovered after it's no longer needed. Establish clear triggers for disposal - end of retention period, project completion, contract termination, or explicit disposal request. Create procedures to identify all instances of confidential information scheduled for destruction, including primary copies, backups, archives, and copies on employee devices. For electronic data, use appropriate destruction methods based on sensitivity - simple deletion for low-risk data, secure overwriting for moderate risk, and physical destruction or cryptographic erasure for high-risk data. For physical documents, use cross-cut shredding or certified destruction services. Maintain detailed records of destruction including what was destroyed, when, how, by whom, and under what authority. Obtain certificates of destruction from third-party services. Verify destruction is complete by checking all storage locations including backup systems. Implement procedures to handle mixed media (like hard drives in copiers) and ensure destruction methods are appropriate for the medium. Regular audits verify disposal procedures are followed consistently. Consider regulatory requirements that may override normal disposal schedules.

Implementation: S3 lifecycle rules and the scheduled retention-enforcement Lambda delete data at the end of its retention period; KMS key deletion provides cryptographic erasure, per the Data Retention and Disposal Policy. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys, AWS S3 Buckets.
notes: Implementation: specific; Retention-enforcement Lambda named from the R4 table.

name: CC1.1.1 Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal Code of Conduct that articulates the ethical standards and behavioral expectations applicable to all personnel, including employees, contractors, and business partners. This document shall define acceptable conduct regarding integrity, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and professional behavior. The Code of Conduct must be approved by leadership, communicated to all relevant parties, and made readily accessible. Given the remote work environment, the document shall address ethical considerations specific to distributed teams, including data handling outside traditional office settings and professional conduct in virtual communications.

Implementation: The Code of Conduct covers integrity, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and remote-work conduct; it is approved by the CEO and acknowledged annually by all personnel in the compliance platform portal.
notes: Implementation: specific; Acknowledgment mechanism per R6.

name: CC1.1.2 Leadership Commitment and Tone at the Top
description:
Executive leadership shall demonstrate visible commitment to integrity and ethical values through documented communications, decision-making practices, and organizational governance. Leadership must formally endorse the Code of Conduct and ethical standards, communicate expectations through regular channels, and model appropriate behavior. This includes leadership participation in ethics-related discussions during team meetings, documented responses to ethical concerns, and consistent enforcement of standards. Leadership shall conduct periodic reviews of ethical compliance and address any identified concerns promptly and consistently to reinforce the importance of ethical conduct throughout the organization.

Implementation: The CEO signed the Code of Conduct and completed security training; both are recorded in the compliance platform. Evidence: Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC1.1.3 Ethics Training and Awareness Program
description:
The organization shall implement a training and awareness program to ensure all personnel understand their ethical obligations and the standards set forth in the Code of Conduct. Training shall be provided upon onboarding and on an annual basis thereafter. The program must cover key topics including integrity expectations, reporting mechanisms for ethical concerns, consequences of violations, and specific considerations for remote work environments. Training completion shall be tracked and documented, with remediation procedures for personnel who do not complete required training within established timeframes.

Implementation: Ethics and security-awareness training is completed in the compliance platform at onboarding and annually; the current certificates are dated December 9, 2025. Evidence: Ethics And Privacy Training Completion Certificate William Wickey, Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi.
notes: Implementation: specific; Date format per Q2.

name: CC1.1.4 Ethics Violation Reporting and Response Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for reporting suspected ethical violations and responding to such reports in a timely and consistent manner. A confidential reporting mechanism shall be made available to all personnel, enabling them to raise concerns without fear of retaliation. All reported concerns shall be documented, investigated appropriately, and resolved with documented outcomes. Disciplinary actions for confirmed violations shall be applied consistently in accordance with established policies. The organization shall ensure reporting channels maintain appropriate confidentiality while enabling effective investigation and resolution.

Implementation: Reporting and investigation steps are set out in the Code of Conduct; reports are recorded in the ethics violation log, which shows zero violations in 2025. Evidence: Ethics Violation Log 2025.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC1.1 The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
description:
CC1.1 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.

Your organization needs to establish and communicate clear expectations for ethical behavior throughout the company. This starts with leadership setting the right tone from the top - showing through actions that integrity matters. Create a code of conduct that defines expected behavior for employees, contractors, and business partners. Train everyone on these standards and make sure they understand them. Regularly evaluate whether people are following the rules through reviews, audits, or observations. When violations occur, address them quickly and consistently to show that ethics policies have teeth. Controls must cover all stakeholders who interact with the organization's systems and data.

Implementation: The Code of Conduct is signed by all personnel; training completed in 2025 (CEO 8 hours security, Go-to-Market Contractor 4 hours privacy) and the ethics violation log shows zero violations. Evidence: Ethics And Privacy Training Completion Certificate William Wickey, Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi, Ethics Violation Log 2025.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: role; "contractor" -> Go-to-Market Contractor; "signed by all" -> all personnel.

name: CC1.2.1 Designation of Independent Oversight Authority
description:
The organization shall formally designate an independent oversight authority responsible for governance of the security and compliance program. This authority may be an external advisor, board member, or senior executive who maintains independence from day-to-day IT and security operations. The designated authority must possess or have access to relevant expertise in security, privacy, and technology matters. This designation shall be documented in writing, clearly articulating the scope of oversight responsibilities, reporting relationships, and the basis for determining independence from operational management.

Implementation: The CEO provides oversight with consultation from an external advisor; the arrangement is documented in the organizational structure and the management meeting minutes. Evidence: Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025, Organizational Structure.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: confirm; Independence basis and the external advisor are v1 claims; CONFIRM.

name: CC1.2.2 Periodic Independent Oversight Reviews
description:
The designated independent oversight authority shall conduct periodic reviews of the organization's internal control environment, security posture, and management's performance in executing control activities. These reviews shall occur at a frequency appropriate to the organization's risk profile, but no less than annually. The oversight authority shall document their review activities, findings, and any recommendations for improvement. Management shall be required to respond to identified deficiencies and report on remediation progress. Review sessions shall include examination of control effectiveness, security incidents, compliance status, and any material changes to the risk environment.

Implementation: Quarterly management meetings review security posture, incidents, and compliance status; the Q4 2025 meeting is minuted. Evidence: Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025.
notes: Implementation: role; Board -> management meeting (R2).

name: CC1.2 The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development an
description:
CC1.2 (CC1 - Control Environment): The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.

Someone independent from day-to-day operations must oversee your security and compliance program. This oversight body needs to understand and accept their responsibilities for internal controls. They should have (or obtain through advisors) relevant expertise in security, privacy, and technology to ask probing questions and challenge management. This might be an outside advisor, board member, or senior executive who isn't directly involved in IT operations. They need sufficient independence to objectively evaluate controls and management's performance. Consider bringing in specialized consultants if your board lacks technical security expertise. Regular oversight reviews should examine whether controls are working as intended.

Implementation: The Q4 2025 management meeting reviewed compliance status, security posture, and control effectiveness. Evidence: Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC1.3.1 Organizational Structure and Reporting Lines Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal documentation of its organizational structure, including clear reporting relationships and lines of authority. This documentation must explicitly define the hierarchy, decision-making authority levels, and communication channels. The structure shall account for all personnel regardless of geographic location and shall be reviewed annually or upon significant organizational changes. Documentation must clearly delineate who reports to whom and establish escalation paths for operational, security, and privacy matters.

Implementation: Reporting lines and escalation paths are documented in the organizational structure. Evidence: Organizational Structure.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: size; "for remote team" removed. Decisions applied: D25.

name: CC1.3.2 Authority Delegation and Segregation of Duties Framework
description:
The organization shall establish a formal framework defining decision-making authorities and responsibilities across all critical functions. This framework must specify approval thresholds for system access provisioning, change authorization, incident response decisions, and privacy-related determinations. The framework shall implement compensating controls where traditional segregation of duties is not feasible, such as enhanced monitoring, management review, and audit trails. The framework must address vendor and third-party relationship management, clearly establishing responsibilities and interaction protocols with external parties.

Implementation: Job descriptions define decision authority for each role and IAM roles enforce technical access; where duties cannot be segregated, the compensating controls are the pull-request workflow with required CI checks, CloudTrail logging, and the external auditor's review. Evidence: Job Description Chief Executive Officer, Job Description Go To Market Contractor.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Compensating controls cited from R2.

name: CC1.3 Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pu
description:
CC1.3 (CC1 - Control Environment): Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

Create clear organizational structures that show reporting relationships and define who has authority for what decisions. Consider all parts of your organization including subsidiaries, remote offices, and outsourced providers. Document who can approve system access, authorize changes, handle incidents, and make privacy decisions. Define responsibilities at appropriate levels - not everything needs CEO approval, but critical decisions shouldn't rest with junior staff. Ensure proper segregation of duties to prevent any one person from having too much control. When working with external parties like vendors or partners, clearly establish their responsibilities and how they interact with your organization. For privacy and security matters, ensure structures support compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

Implementation: The organizational structure defines roles and reporting lines, and the job descriptions specify security responsibilities. Evidence: Job Description Chief Executive Officer, Job Description Go To Market Contractor, Organizational Structure.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC1.4.1 Personnel Competency Requirements and Background Verification
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented competency requirements for all roles, with particular emphasis on positions involving security responsibilities. The organization shall verify professional references and validate claimed qualifications prior to granting access to sensitive systems. This includes defining core security competencies expected of all personnel and ensuring appropriate training is completed before accessing production systems.

Implementation: Competency requirements are set in the job descriptions, professional references are verified, and security training is completed before production access (certificates dated December 9, 2025). Evidence: Ethics And Privacy Training Completion Certificate William Wickey, Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi, Job Description Chief Executive Officer, Job Description Go To Market Contractor.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none; Date format.

name: CC1.4.2 Security Training Program and Competency Development
description:
The organization shall implement a security awareness and training program that provides initial onboarding training on security policies and procedures, followed by ongoing education to maintain current knowledge of security practices. Training shall address remote work security considerations, data protection responsibilities, and role-specific security requirements. The organization shall maintain training records demonstrating completion and shall periodically evaluate personnel competence, addressing identified gaps through additional training or mentoring. Succession planning considerations for critical roles shall be documented to ensure continuity of operations.

Implementation: Security-awareness training is completed in the compliance platform at onboarding and annually, and security responsibilities are assessed in the annual performance evaluation. Evidence: Annual Performance Evaluation Ceo.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Training mechanism per R4 table.

name: CC1.4 The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with o
description:
CC1.4 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with objectives.

Build and maintain a team with the skills needed to protect data and systems. Establish clear competency requirements for each role, especially those involving security responsibilities. Check backgrounds of employees and contractors before granting access to sensitive systems - the depth of checking should match the sensitivity of the role. Provide initial training on security policies and ongoing education to keep skills current. Evaluate competence regularly and address gaps through training, mentoring, or hiring. Have succession plans for critical roles so you're not scrambling if someone leaves suddenly. Consider the technical competency of vendors and their employees too. Maintain training records to demonstrate your commitment to competence.

Implementation: Training completed in 2025: CEO 8 hours, Go-to-Market Contractor 4 hours; certificates dated December 9, 2025 are held in the compliance platform. Evidence: Ethics And Privacy Training Completion Certificate William Wickey, Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: role.

name: CC1.5.1 Security Responsibilities in Role Definitions
description:
The organization shall formally document security and compliance responsibilities within job descriptions, employment agreements, and role expectations for all personnel. Security accountabilities for each role must be explicitly defined and communicated during onboarding and annually thereafter. This includes clear delineation of data handling responsibilities, access management duties, incident reporting obligations, and compliance requirements specific to each role.

Implementation: Security responsibilities are documented in each job description and reviewed in the annual performance evaluation. Evidence: PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: confirm; Linked evidence (PropelAuth Security Settings) does not match the control; CONFIRM link.

name: CC1.5.2 Performance Evaluation and Accountability Measures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for evaluating personnel performance against security and compliance objectives. Performance assessments must incorporate security-related criteria, including adherence to policies, completion of required training, and contribution to the organization's security posture. A documented sanctions process shall be maintained for addressing non-compliance, ranging from remedial training to disciplinary action, applied consistently across all personnel. This process should be proportionate and focused on improvement while maintaining clear consequences for willful violations.

Implementation: Personnel MFA is enforced in AWS (the IAM credential report shows 100 % MFA) and in Google Workspace and GitHub; customer sign-in is Google SSO through PropelAuth, which inherits Google Workspace MFA. The annual performance evaluation assesses security responsibilities. Evidence: Annual Performance Evaluation Ceo, AWS IAM Users, PropelAuth Users.

name: CC1.5 The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objecti
description:
CC1.5 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

Create accountability for security and control responsibilities throughout your organization. Clearly communicate what's expected through job descriptions, policies, and regular reinforcement. Establish performance measures that include security and compliance responsibilities - make it clear these aren't optional extras. Set up incentives and rewards that encourage good security behavior while being careful not to create pressures that might lead to corner-cutting. Evaluate performance regularly, looking at both adherence to policies and achievement of security objectives. When people don't meet expectations, take appropriate action ranging from additional training to disciplinary measures. For privacy-related violations, have a defined sanctions process that's consistently applied. Balance accountability with reasonable expectations - don't create impossible standards that encourage workarounds.

Implementation: Customer sign-in is Google SSO through PropelAuth; IAM roles enforce least privilege in AWS; quarterly access reviews are minuted in the management meeting. Evidence: AWS IAM Users, Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025, PropelAuth Security Settings, PropelAuth Users.

name: CC2.1.1 IT Asset Inventory Management
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a comprehensive inventory of all information technology assets utilized in business operations. This inventory must encompass hardware devices (including employee-owned devices used for work purposes), software applications, cloud services, and data repositories. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be paid to documenting assets located at employee residences and third-party vendor locations. The inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to ensure accuracy and completeness. Each asset entry shall include, at minimum: asset identifier, description, owner, location, and criticality classification.

Implementation: The AWS asset inventory (8 Lambda functions, 1 DocumentDB cluster, S3 buckets, VPC) is exported with the AWS CLI and refreshed annually. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Cluster, AWS Lambda Functions, AWS S3 Buckets, AWS VPC List.
notes: Implementation: role; Board -> management. Decisions applied: D25.

name: CC2.1.2 Information Classification and Data Flow Documentation
description:
The organization shall implement a formal information classification scheme that categorizes all organizational data according to sensitivity levels (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted). Data flow documentation shall be created and maintained to illustrate how information traverses organizational systems, including transfers to and from remote employee environments and external service providers. Classification labels shall be applied consistently across all data repositories and communications. Personnel shall receive guidance on handling requirements for each classification level. This documentation shall be reviewed annually or upon significant changes to systems or business processes.

Implementation: Data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted under the Data Classification and Handling Standard, and data flows are documented in the system description. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys.

name: CC2.1 The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal
description:
CC2.1 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.

Maintain comprehensive, accurate information about your systems and controls to support good decision-making. Start by identifying what information you need to manage security effectively. Document data flows showing how information moves through your systems. Create and maintain an inventory of all IT assets including hardware, software, and data repositories. Classify information by sensitivity level (public, internal, confidential, restricted) to apply appropriate protections. Track where data is stored, including data on employee devices or at vendor locations. Ensure the information you use for security decisions is timely, accurate, complete, and protected from tampering. Review information quality regularly - outdated asset inventories or incorrect data classifications can lead to security gaps.

Implementation: The asset inventory (Lambda functions, DocumentDB, S3 buckets) is exported with the AWS CLI; handling rules per tier are in the Data Classification and Handling Standard. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Cluster, AWS Lambda Functions, AWS S3 Buckets.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC2.2.1 Internal Security Communication Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal framework for communicating security-related information to all personnel. This framework must define communication channels, frequency, and methods appropriate for a remote workforce. This may be consolidated into regular team communications but must ensure all personnel receive timely updates regarding security objectives, policy changes, control responsibilities, and their individual duties in maintaining the security posture. Communication methods shall be documented and consistently applied across the distributed team.

Implementation: Security objectives, policy changes, and control responsibilities are communicated through policy acknowledgments in the compliance platform portal and the quarterly management meeting.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: confirm; v1 "regular team communications" is generic; mechanism named from R6/R8 (portal) and R2 (management meeting). CONFIRM.

name: CC2.2.2 Security Awareness Training Program
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain a security awareness training program that educates all personnel on recognizing and responding to security threats. Training content must address the specific risks associated with remote work environments, including phishing, social engineering, secure handling of company data, and proper use of collaboration tools. Training shall be conducted upon hire and at least annually thereafter, with completion tracked and documented. For personnel handling personal information, training must include specific guidance on privacy requirements and proper data handling procedures.

Implementation: Security-awareness training is completed in the compliance platform at onboarding and annually; completion certificates are the evidence.
notes: Implementation: specific; Per R4 table; no task linked (certificates are linked to CC1.1.3/CC1.4).

name: CC2.2.3 Incident and Concern Reporting Mechanisms
description:
The organization shall establish clear, accessible mechanisms for personnel to report system failures, security incidents, policy violations, and other concerns. Reporting procedures must be straightforward and well-communicated. The organization shall maintain a non-punitive reporting culture that encourages prompt disclosure of issues. A confidential reporting channel shall be available for sensitive matters. All personnel must be informed of how to utilize these reporting mechanisms, and management shall ensure timely acknowledgment and response to all reports received.

Implementation: Personnel report incidents and concerns to the CEO as set out in the Incident Response Procedure and the Code of Conduct; reports are recorded in the compliance platform incident register.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Incident register per R4 ("compliance platform is the control register").

name: CC2.2 The entity internally communicates information necessary to support the functioning of internal control.
description:
CC2.2 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity internally communicates information necessary to support the functioning of internal control.

Establish effective internal communication to ensure everyone understands and can fulfill their security responsibilities. Communicate control responsibilities clearly to all personnel, including what's expected and how to carry out their duties. Keep staff informed about security objectives and any changes to those objectives. Share information about how to report system failures, security incidents, and other concerns - make reporting easy and non-punitive. Implement security awareness training that teaches employees to recognize and respond to threats. Ensure communication flows both up and down - management needs to hear about problems, and staff need to understand priorities. Provide separate, confidential channels (like anonymous hotlines) for sensitive reports. Choose communication methods that fit your audience - technical details for IT staff, practical guidance for general users. For privacy programs, include specific training on handling personal information properly.

Implementation: The Information Security Policy is acknowledged by all personnel in the compliance platform portal, training is completed annually, and reporting steps are in the Incident Response Procedure.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC2.3.1 External Security Communication Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal communication channels and documentation for conveying security-related information to external parties. This includes the publication of a comprehensive privacy notice on the company website, maintenance of security documentation for customer inquiries, and establishment of vendor security requirements. All external-facing security communications shall be reviewed and approved by appropriate personnel prior to publication or distribution.

Implementation: The privacy notice is published on dealintelligence.io and security documentation is provided to customers on request after CEO review.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC2.3.2 External Security Reporting Mechanism
description:
The organization shall provide and maintain accessible mechanisms for external parties to report security concerns, vulnerabilities, or incidents. This includes establishing a dedicated security contact point (e.g., security@company.com), publishing responsible disclosure guidelines where appropriate, and implementing procedures for timely acknowledgment and response to external security reports. All reported concerns shall be documented, triaged, and addressed in accordance with established incident response procedures.

Implementation: External parties report security concerns to the security contact published in the privacy notice; reports are triaged under the Incident Response Procedure, and the DPA template defines vendor notification duties.
notes: Implementation: confirm; v1 names no contact address; CONFIRM the published security contact.

name: CC2.3 The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.
description:
CC2.3 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.

Communicate appropriately with customers, vendors, regulators, and other external parties about your security practices. This includes publishing privacy notices, sharing security requirements with vendors, responding to customer security inquiries, and providing ways for external parties to report security concerns or incidents.

Implementation: The privacy notice is published, a security contact is available to external parties, and security requirements for vendors are set in the DPA template.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC3.1.1 Security Program Objectives Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal document that articulates the security program objectives with sufficient clarity and specificity. This document shall define the organization's goals for protecting customer data, maintaining system availability, safeguarding confidential information, and meeting GDPR and CCPA obligations. The objectives shall be aligned with business operations, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder expectations. Given the organization's remote work environment, objectives shall specifically address distributed workforce security considerations. The document shall be reviewed and approved by leadership annually or upon significant changes to the business environment.

Implementation: Security objectives are stated in the Risk Assessment Procedure and reviewed annually by the CEO; the compliance platform risk register holds 7 risks across categories. Evidence: Compliance Platform Risk Register.
notes: Requirement: R1 edit(s). Implementation: humadroid, r5; Risk count 6 -> 7 (current register export).

name: CC3.1.2 Risk Identification Framework Based on Defined Objectives
description:
The organization shall implement a structured approach to identify and assess risks that could impede the achievement of documented security objectives. This framework shall enable systematic identification of threats and vulnerabilities across all Trust Services Criteria domains relevant to the organization's operations. The risk identification process shall consider the unique risk profile associated with a fully remote technology organization, including distributed access points, cloud infrastructure dependencies, and remote collaboration tools. Risk assessments shall be conducted at least annually and upon material changes to systems, processes, or the operating environment.

Implementation: The monthly configuration-check record, real-time security-event alerts from CloudTrail via EventBridge, and the annual risk assessment identify threats; the compliance platform tracks each risk by category with severity scoring. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), Compliance Platform Risk Register.
notes: Implementation: humadroid. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.1 The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable identification and assessment of risks.
description:
CC3.1 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable identification and assessment of risks.

Define clear goals for what you're trying to protect and achieve with your security program. These objectives should cover protecting customer data, maintaining system availability, and keeping confidential information secret. Clear objectives help you identify what could go wrong and where to focus your security efforts.

Implementation: The Risk Assessment Procedure documents objectives and the identification method; the compliance platform risk register tracks 7 identified risks. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), Compliance Platform Risk Register.
notes: Requirement: R1 edit(s). Implementation: humadroid, r5; Risk count 6 -> 7. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.2.1 Enterprise Risk Assessment Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal risk assessment framework that identifies, analyzes, and evaluates risks to the achievement of business objectives. This framework shall encompass enterprise-wide risks as well as risks specific to systems, processes, and operations. The assessment shall consider both internal factors (personnel errors, system failures, process deficiencies) and external factors (cyber threats, natural disasters, regulatory changes). Risk assessments shall be conducted at least annually or upon significant changes to the business environment, with appropriate management involvement to ensure business context is properly considered in risk tolerance decisions.

Implementation: The Risk Assessment Procedure covers enterprise, system, and process risks from internal and external factors; the compliance platform scores risks using the Multi-Impact Assessment method. Evidence: Compliance Platform Risk Detail.
notes: Implementation: humadroid.

name: CC3.2.2 Third-Party and Vendor Risk Evaluation
description:
The organization shall identify and assess risks arising from vendors, business partners, and other third parties with access to organizational systems or data. This evaluation shall be integrated into the overall risk assessment process and shall consider the nature and extent of third-party access, the sensitivity of data or systems involved, and the potential impact of third-party failures or breaches. Risk treatment decisions for third-party relationships shall be documented and reviewed periodically to ensure continued appropriateness as business relationships evolve.

Implementation: The compliance platform vendor register holds 5 vendors with risk tiers: AWS and PropelAuth as sub-processors, and GitHub, Google Workspace, and Resend as vendors that do not process customer data; SOC 2 reports are checked in the vendor assessment. Evidence: Compliance Platform Vendor Assessment, Compliance Platform Vendor Dashboard.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, r5; Vendor count 2 -> 5 (current vendor export). Decisions applied: D15.

name: CC3.2 The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives and analyzes risks as a basis for determining
description:
CC3.2 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives and analyzes risks as a basis for determining how the risks should be managed.

Conduct comprehensive risk assessments covering all levels of your organization - from enterprise-wide risks down to specific systems and processes. Consider both internal factors (employee errors, system failures, process gaps) and external factors (hackers, natural disasters, regulatory changes). Identify specific threats to your objectives and the vulnerabilities that could be exploited. Pay special attention to risks from vendors, business partners, and other third parties with system access. Involve appropriate management levels in risk assessment - they understand business context and can make informed decisions about risk tolerance. Estimate the likelihood and potential impact of each risk to prioritize your response. Decide how to handle each risk: accept it (if impact is low), avoid it (stop the risky activity), reduce it (implement controls), or transfer it (through insurance or contracts). Document your risk assessment process and review it regularly as threats evolve.

Implementation: The CEO performs the annual risk assessment; each risk carries a likelihood and impact score in the compliance platform risk detail. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), Compliance Platform Risk Detail.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, confirm; v1 example "4/3 = score 32" dropped (arithmetic does not match); CONFIRM the scoring formula. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.3.1 Fraud Risk Assessment and Documentation
description:
The organization shall conduct and document a formal fraud risk assessment that identifies potential fraud scenarios relevant to its operations. This assessment must evaluate the fraud triangle elements (incentive/pressure, opportunity, and rationalization) for both internal and external threat actors. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to risks associated with distributed access to systems, data exfiltration opportunities, and the reduced oversight inherent in remote operations. The assessment shall be reviewed and updated annually or upon significant organizational changes.

Implementation: The fraud triangle is evaluated in the annual risk assessment; the People Risk entry in the compliance platform records a Mitigate treatment with documented actions. Evidence: Compliance Platform Risk Detail.
notes: Implementation: humadroid.

name: CC3.3.2 Fraud Prevention Controls and Monitoring
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain controls designed to prevent and detect fraudulent activities, including unauthorized system modifications, data theft, asset misappropriation, and falsification of records. Controls shall include segregation of duties where practicable, access logging and review procedures, and mechanisms for reporting suspected fraudulent activity. Management shall establish clear accountability for fraud prevention oversight and ensure all personnel understand their responsibilities in maintaining the integrity of organizational systems and data.

Implementation: CloudTrail logs all API activity; security-relevant events (root sign-in, IAM policy or user changes, CloudTrail stop/delete, KMS key disable, security-group changes) trigger an EventBridge rule to the breach-detection Lambda, which alerts the CEO via SNS in real time, and the monthly configuration-check Lambda records a pass/fail checklist in the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails, Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r4; GuardDuty removed (R4); detection = CloudTrail + EventBridge security-event rule + breach-detection Lambda, and the monthly configuration-check Lambda (D12). Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.3 The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks.
description:
CC3.3 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks.

Think about how someone might intentionally misuse their access or manipulate your systems for personal gain. Consider both external threats and insider risks, including theft of data or assets, unauthorized system changes, and falsification of records. Look at what might motivate fraud, what opportunities exist, and how someone might justify their actions.

Implementation: Fraud risk is assessed under the Risk Assessment Procedure; the compliance platform risk register includes a People Risk category covering insider threats. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), Compliance Platform Risk Register.
notes: Implementation: humadroid. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.4.1 Change Identification and Monitoring Process
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for identifying and monitoring changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control. This process shall encompass monitoring of regulatory and compliance landscape changes, business operational changes including growth or restructuring, technology infrastructure and application modifications, personnel changes particularly in key security and compliance roles, third-party vendor relationships and service provider changes, and emerging threat intelligence relevant to the organization's technology sector. This process shall be streamlined yet comprehensive, with designated responsibility for change monitoring assigned to appropriate personnel.

Implementation: The monthly configuration-check Lambda and the CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule flag configuration changes, Dependabot and ECR scan-on-push flag new vulnerabilities, and the CEO reviews vendor, regulatory, and personnel changes in the quarterly risk review. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Quarterly risk review from the CC3.4 note. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC3.4.2 Change Impact Assessment and Control Adequacy Review
description:
The organization shall implement a structured methodology for assessing the impact of identified changes on the existing risk profile and evaluating whether current internal controls remain adequate. For each significant change identified, the organization shall conduct a documented impact assessment that evaluates the effect on existing risks, identifies new risks introduced by the change, determines whether existing controls sufficiently address modified or new risks, and recommends control modifications or new controls as necessary. Assessment frequency shall be commensurate with the pace of change, with immediate assessment triggered for material changes and periodic reviews conducted at minimum on a quarterly basis. Given the organization's remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to changes affecting remote access, collaboration tools, and distributed workforce security controls.

Implementation: Change triggers and the quarterly review cadence are set in the Risk Assessment Procedure; each quarterly risk review is recorded as a snapshot in the compliance platform risk register.
notes: Implementation: specific; Quarterly snapshot from the CC3.4 note.

name: CC3.4 The entity identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control.
description:
CC3.4 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control.

Stay alert to changes that could affect your security posture - new regulations, business growth, technology updates, staff turnover, new vendors, or emerging threats. Have a process to evaluate how these changes impact your risks and whether your existing controls are still adequate. Regular assessment helps prevent security gaps during transitions.

Implementation: The CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule and the monthly configuration-check Lambda detect significant configuration changes, and the Q4 2025 risk snapshot in the compliance platform records the quarterly risk review. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), Compliance Platform Risk Register.
notes: Implementation: humadroid. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC4.1.1 Internal Control Monitoring Program
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal program for ongoing monitoring of internal controls. This program shall define the scope of controls subject to evaluation, assign responsibility for monitoring activities, and establish a risk-based schedule for assessments. Monitoring activities should be streamlined yet comprehensive, with clear ownership assigned to designated personnel. The program shall include both continuous monitoring mechanisms (such as automated alerts and log reviews) and periodic assessments appropriate to the organization's risk profile.

Implementation: CloudWatch alarms and log reviews provide continuous monitoring, and the compliance platform is the control register for periodic control evaluation. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events, Lambda App Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific.

name: CC4.1.2 Security Control Testing and Evaluation
description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing and evaluation of security controls to verify their operational effectiveness. Testing activities shall include, at minimum, annual vulnerability assessments via automated scanning tools, annual access log reviews, and periodic verification of critical security configurations. For a remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to evaluating controls related to remote access, endpoint security, and cloud service configurations. Deficiencies identified through testing shall be documented, prioritized based on risk, and remediated within established timeframes.

Implementation: ECR scan-on-push, Dependabot and code scanning, and Trivy in CI provide continuous vulnerability scanning (21 Dependabot alerts tracked), the configuration-check Lambda runs monthly, an annual third-party penetration test is performed, and the quarterly access review is minuted in the management meeting. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, Configuration-check record (monthly), Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025.
notes: Implementation: r4, r5; GuardDuty removed; annual access review -> quarterly (R5); pen test from R3. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC4.1 The entity selects, develops, and performs ongoing evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal
description:
CC4.1 (CC4 - Monitoring Activities): The entity selects, develops, and performs ongoing evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal control are present and functioning.

Regularly check that your security controls actually work as intended. This includes routine monitoring like reviewing access logs, as well as periodic assessments like penetration tests or compliance audits. Choose evaluation methods that match your risk level - high-risk areas need more frequent and thorough testing.

Implementation: CloudWatch and the CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule provide continuous monitoring, the configuration-check Lambda posts a monthly pass/fail record, and the scheduled access-review Lambda performs periodic reviews. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS Lambda Functions, Configuration-check record (monthly), CloudTrail Events, Lambda App Events.
notes: Implementation: r4; GuardDuty removed. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC4.2.1 Internal Control Deficiency Documentation and Tracking
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for documenting, categorizing, and tracking internal control deficiencies from identification through remediation. All identified security weaknesses and control gaps must be recorded in a centralized tracking system with appropriate severity classifications, assigned ownership, and target remediation dates. The tracking mechanism shall capture the nature of the deficiency, potential impact, root cause analysis, and corrective action plans. A streamlined approach utilizing existing project management or issue tracking tools is acceptable, provided all requisite information is captured and maintained.

Implementation: Failed items in the monthly configuration-check record and security-event alerts carry a severity, an owner (the CEO), and a remediation date; they are reviewed monthly and tracked in the compliance platform. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Monthly review per R5. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC4.2.2 Deficiency Communication and Escalation Procedures
description:
The organization shall implement formal communication and escalation procedures to ensure internal control deficiencies are reported to appropriate parties in a timely manner commensurate with their severity. Critical and high-severity deficiencies must be escalated to senior management within defined timeframes. Regular status reporting on the overall state of the security program and outstanding deficiencies shall be provided to leadership. Communication protocols should leverage established digital communication channels while ensuring appropriate documentation of all escalations and management acknowledgments.

Implementation: Security-relevant CloudTrail events alert the CEO in real time via EventBridge, the breach-detection Lambda, and SNS; the configuration-check record is reviewed monthly, and program status is reported in the quarterly management meeting. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Escalation mechanism from R4/R5. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC4.2 The entity evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties respon
description:
CC4.2 (CC4 - Monitoring Activities): The entity evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties responsible for taking corrective action.

When security weaknesses are found, document them clearly, communicate them to the right people, and track them until they're fixed. Ensure serious issues escalate to senior management quickly, and keep leadership informed about the overall state of your security program. Learn from deficiencies to prevent similar issues in the future.

Implementation: The monthly configuration-check record and real-time security-event alerts identify deficiencies, CloudWatch Logs and CloudTrail support investigation, and remediation is tracked in the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, Configuration-check record (monthly), CloudTrail Events.
notes: Implementation: none. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC5.1.1 Risk-Based Control Selection and Documentation
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal process for selecting and documenting security controls based on identified risks. Control selection must demonstrate clear alignment between specific risks and chosen mitigations, with documented rationale for each control's inclusion. The selection process shall consider cost-effectiveness, operational impact, and the organization's remote work environment. A control inventory shall be maintained that maps each control to its corresponding risk(s) and categorizes controls as preventive or detective, and technical or procedural.

Implementation: Controls are mapped to risks in the compliance platform; IAM roles and KMS encryption are the preventive access and data controls. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC5.1.2 Balanced Control Framework Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement a balanced portfolio of security controls that includes both preventive measures (such as access restrictions, encryption, and authentication requirements) and detective measures (such as logging, monitoring, and periodic reviews). Given the remote work environment, particular emphasis shall be placed on controls that address distributed workforce risks. The control framework shall ensure adequate coverage across technical safeguards (automated systems and tools) and procedural safeguards (policies, training, and manual processes).

Implementation: Detective controls are CloudWatch alarms, CloudTrail, the monthly configuration-check Lambda, and the EventBridge security-event rule that routes security-relevant CloudTrail events through the breach-detection Lambda to SNS. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r4; GuardDuty removed. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC5.1 The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achieveme
description:
CC5.1 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achievement of objectives to acceptable levels.

Choose security controls that effectively address your identified risks without being overly complex or expensive. Mix preventive controls (like access restrictions) with detective controls (like monitoring), and ensure you have both technical and procedural safeguards. Focus on controls that give you the best risk reduction for your investment.

Implementation: Preventive controls: IAM and KMS; detective: CloudWatch, CloudTrail with the EventBridge security-event rule, and the monthly configuration-check Lambda; corrective: the Incident Response Procedure and Lambda versioned rollback. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS IAM Roles, AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Implementation: r4; GuardDuty removed; rollback mechanism from R4. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC5.2.1 IT Infrastructure and Access Management
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal controls over IT infrastructure and administrative access. This includes implementing role-based access controls for all critical systems, maintaining an inventory of IT assets, restricting administrative privileges to authorized personnel only, and ensuring secure configuration of network infrastructure. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be paid to secure remote access mechanisms and endpoint security controls.

Implementation: Infrastructure is defined in CloudFormation and deployed through the Serverless Framework, so every deployment is version-controlled; the CEO is the only role with administrative access. Evidence: AWS Cloudformation Stacks.
notes: Implementation: role.

name: CC5.2.2 Change Management and Software Development Controls
description:
The organization shall implement formal change management procedures governing modifications to IT systems, applications, and infrastructure. All changes shall be documented, reviewed, tested, and approved prior to implementation in production environments. This includes establishing separation of duties where feasible, maintaining version control for all code and configurations, and ensuring changes are traceable and reversible. Emergency change procedures shall be documented for time-sensitive situations.

Implementation: All changes go through a pull request on the protected main branch with required CI status checks and a logged self-review; emergency changes use a PR labelled emergency with post-hoc review within 5 business days. Evidence: GitHub Branch Protection.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; "PR approval required" -> PR + CI gate + self-review (R2/R3); emergency path per R5.

name: CC5.2.3 Technology Acquisition and Security Assessment
description:
The organization shall establish procedures to ensure that technology acquisitions, including software, hardware, and cloud services, meet defined security requirements prior to deployment. This includes conducting security assessments of new vendors and technologies, reviewing security certifications and compliance attestations, and ensuring contractual provisions address security obligations. Given the company's technology industry context, particular scrutiny shall be applied to third-party components and dependencies.

Implementation: New vendors and technologies are assessed in the compliance platform vendor assessment before use, under the Vendor Management Policy.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC5.2 The entity selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objec
description:
CC5.2 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives.

Implement fundamental IT controls that support all your systems and applications. This includes managing IT infrastructure, controlling software changes, restricting administrative access, maintaining system configurations, and ensuring technology acquisitions meet security requirements. These foundational controls support everything else you do.

Implementation: Infrastructure is deployed as code with CloudFormation, and GitHub branch protection requires a pull request with passing CI status checks before merge. Evidence: GitHub Deploy Workflow, GitHub Branch Protection, AWS Cloudformation Stacks.
notes: Implementation: r5; "enforces code review" -> PR + CI gate.

name: CC5.3.1 Security Policy Documentation and Procedural Framework
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal framework that translates approved security policies into documented operational procedures. Each policy shall have corresponding step-by-step procedures that specify the actions required for implementation, the personnel responsible for execution, and the timelines for completion of critical tasks. Procedures shall be written in clear, actionable language appropriate for the intended audience and shall be readily accessible to all relevant personnel through the organization's document management system.

Implementation: Each policy has an operating procedure (Access Control, Change Management, Incident Response) published in the compliance platform portal and accessible to all personnel.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC5.3.2 Control Activity Competency and Authorization
description:
The organization shall ensure that personnel assigned to execute control activities possess the requisite skills, knowledge, and formal authorization to perform their designated responsibilities. This includes maintaining documentation of role assignments, ensuring appropriate training has been completed, and verifying that personnel have been granted the necessary system access and decision-making authority. Given the organization's remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to ensuring personnel can effectively execute controls independent of physical location.

Implementation: Role competencies are set in the job descriptions, training completion is recorded in the compliance platform, and IAM grants access to the CEO only.
notes: Implementation: role.

name: CC5.3.3 Periodic Review of Control Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish a formal review cycle to assess the continued relevance and effectiveness of documented procedures. Reviews shall be conducted at least annually, or more frequently when significant changes occur to the business environment, technology infrastructure, or regulatory requirements. The review process shall evaluate whether procedures remain aligned with current policies, reflect actual operational practices, and adequately address evolving risks. Findings from reviews shall be documented and result in timely updates to affected procedures.

Implementation: Policies and procedures are reviewed annually by the CEO; the review was minuted in the Q4 2025 management meeting and the next review is due Q4 2026. Evidence: Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025.
notes: Implementation: role; Board -> management.

name: CC5.3 The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and in procedures that
description:
CC5.3 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and in procedures that put policies into action.

Turn your security policies into practical procedures that people can actually follow. Document step-by-step processes, assign clear responsibilities, set timelines for critical tasks, ensure staff have the skills and authority to perform controls, and regularly review whether procedures still make sense as your business evolves.

Implementation: Policies are put into practice through the Access Control and Authentication Policy, Change Management Policy, and Incident Response Procedure, all published in the compliance platform portal.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC6.1.1 Information Asset Inventory and Classification
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a comprehensive inventory of all information assets requiring protection, including infrastructure components, software applications, and data repositories. Each asset shall be classified according to its sensitivity and criticality to business operations. This inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to ensure accuracy and completeness. Asset classification shall inform the application of appropriate security controls and access restrictions.
