Implementation: User accounts are inventoried in PropelAuth, the IAM credential report shows 100 % MFA, and the asset inventory is refreshed annually. Evidence: PropelAuth Security Settings, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Implementation: role; Board -> management. Decisions applied: D25.

name: CC6.1.2 Logical Access Control Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement logical access controls to restrict system and data access based on the principle of least privilege and role-based access requirements. Access control software and configurations shall enforce authentication requirements prior to granting access to protected resources. Multi-factor authentication shall be required for all remote access, administrative functions, and access to sensitive data. Access rules shall be documented and aligned with data classification levels and approved user roles.

Implementation: Customer sign-in is Google SSO through PropelAuth; the IAM password policy requires 14+ characters, complexity, and 90-day rotation, and personnel MFA is enforced in AWS, GitHub, and Google Workspace. Evidence: AWS IAM Password Policy, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Implementation: r5; MFA wording per R5; password facts kept from v1.

name: CC6.1.3 Network Security and Segmentation
description:
The organization shall implement network security controls to protect information assets from unauthorized access and security threats. Given the remote work environment, all network communications shall be secured through appropriate encryption and access controls. Network architecture shall incorporate segmentation or zero-trust principles to limit the potential impact of security incidents. All access points, including APIs and remote connections, shall be identified, documented, and secured with appropriate controls.

Implementation: Workloads run in private VPC subnets with no direct internet access; security groups and network ACLs filter traffic. Evidence: AWS Security Groups, AWS VPC List, AWS VPC Subnets.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.1.4 Encryption and Key Management
description:
The organization shall implement encryption controls to protect sensitive data at rest, in transit, and during processing as appropriate to the risk level. Encryption methods shall be selected based on industry standards and the sensitivity of the data being protected. A formal key management program shall be established to govern the entire lifecycle of cryptographic keys, including generation, storage, distribution, use, rotation, and destruction. Key management procedures shall ensure keys are protected from unauthorized access and disclosure.

Implementation: KMS customer-managed keys (8 keys) with annual rotation encrypt DocumentDB and S3; all S3 buckets have default encryption. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Cluster, AWS KMS Keys, AWS S3 Bucket Encryption.
notes: Implementation: none; Key count kept from v1 (CHANGES.md already carries a KMS inventory CONFIRM).

name: CC6.1.5 Credential and Authentication Management
description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for managing credentials for both user accounts and system/service accounts. Password policies shall enforce complexity, length, and rotation requirements appropriate to the access level granted. Service account credentials shall be secured, documented, and subject to periodic review. Authentication mechanisms shall be configured to protect against common attack vectors including brute force attempts and credential stuffing.

Implementation: IAM roles grant least privilege, the DocumentDB credential is rotated by Secrets Manager, and API keys are rotated per the rotation calendar. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, AWS IAM Users.
notes: Implementation: specific; Rotation facts from R3.

name: CC6.1 The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected infor
description:
CC6.1 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security threats.

Implement comprehensive technical controls to protect your information assets from unauthorized access. Start with a complete inventory of what needs protection - infrastructure, software, and data. Evaluate new system architectures for security before implementation. Use access control software and configuration standards to restrict logical access appropriately. Implement strong authentication, requiring users and systems to prove their identity before accessing resources - use multi-factor authentication for sensitive access. Consider network segmentation or zero-trust architectures to limit the blast radius of any breach. Manage all access points including APIs and remote connections. Establish access rules based on data classification and user roles. Properly manage credentials for both people and system accounts. Encrypt sensitive data at rest, in transit, and during processing when appropriate. Protect encryption keys through their entire lifecycle - generation, storage, use, and destruction. Choose encryption methods appropriate to your risk level.

Implementation: Customer sign-in is Google SSO through PropelAuth; AWS access uses IAM with MFA and the IAM password policy. Evidence: AWS IAM Password Policy, AWS IAM Roles, AWS IAM Users, PropelAuth Security Settings, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Implementation: r5; MFA wording per R5.

name: CC6.2.1 User Access Request and Authorization Process
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal, documented process for requesting and authorizing system access for all internal and external users. Prior to provisioning any system credentials, a written or electronic access request must be submitted specifying the user's identity, role, business justification, and required access levels. All access requests shall be reviewed and approved by an appropriate authority (e.g., department head, system owner, or designated manager) before credentials are issued. The approval process must verify that the requested access aligns with the user's job responsibilities and adheres to the principle of least privilege.

Implementation: Users are registered in PropelAuth; the CEO approves each access request before provisioning, and roles are assigned on least privilege under the Access Control and Authentication Policy. Evidence: PropelAuth Security Settings, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.2.2 User Account Lifecycle Management and Periodic Review
description:
The organization shall implement controls to manage the complete lifecycle of user accounts, including registration, modification, and timely deactivation. A centralized inventory of all user accounts shall be maintained, documenting the user's identity, access privileges, and account status. Access reviews shall be conducted at least annually to verify that all accounts remain necessary and appropriate for users' current roles. Upon termination of employment or change in role, access shall be modified or revoked within one business day. The organization shall maintain documented procedures for offboarding that ensure prompt credential revocation across all systems.

Implementation: PropelAuth holds the user inventory, IAM users have 100 % MFA, access is reviewed quarterly (minuted in the Q4 2025 management meeting), and offboarding revokes access within 1 business day. Evidence: AWS IAM Users, Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Implementation: r5, role; Annual access review -> quarterly (R5).

name: CC6.2 Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorizes new intern
description:
CC6.2 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorizes new internal and external users whose access is administered by the entity.

Before giving anyone access to your systems, verify they're authorized and need that access for their job. Create a formal process for requesting, approving, and setting up new accounts. Regularly review all accounts to ensure they're still needed and immediately disable access when someone leaves or changes roles.

Implementation: PropelAuth registers and authenticates users via Google SSO, and AWS IAM enforces MFA and the password policy. Evidence: AWS IAM Password Policy, PropelAuth Mfa Settings, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Implementation: r5; MFA wording.

name: CC6.3.1 Role-Based Access Control Framework
description:
Establish and maintain a documented role-based access control (RBAC) framework that defines access permissions for each role within the organization. Document the specific access rights required for each role's responsibilities across all systems, applications, and data repositories. Maintain an access matrix that clearly maps roles to permitted resources and access levels. This framework shall serve as the authoritative reference for granting, modifying, and revoking access privileges.

Implementation: PropelAuth roles and IAM roles map each role to its permitted resources and access level. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, PropelAuth Roles.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC6.3.2 Access Authorization and Change Management
description:
Implement formal procedures for authorizing, modifying, and removing access to organizational systems and data. All access requests and changes must be documented and approved by an appropriate authority prior to implementation. The CEO or a delegate approved by the CEO shall approve all access changes. Maintain audit trails of all access provisioning activities, including the requestor, approver, date, and specific access granted or revoked. Ensure timely removal of access upon role changes or employment termination.

Implementation: The CEO approves all access changes; CloudTrail logs IAM changes, PropelAuth logs user provisioning, and access is revoked within 1 business day of termination. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails, AWS IAM Users, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC6.3.3 Segregation of Duties Controls
description:
Identify and document incompatible functions that must be segregated to prevent fraud and errors. Where complete segregation is not feasible, implement compensating controls such as enhanced monitoring, detailed audit logging, and periodic independent review of sensitive transactions. At minimum, ensure that critical functions such as payment initiation and approval, code deployment and review, and administrative access changes involve oversight from more than one individual where possible.

Implementation: Where duties cannot be segregated, the compensating controls are the pull-request workflow with required CI status checks, CloudTrail and CloudWatch logging, and independent review by the external auditor. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, AWS Security Groups.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Compensating controls cited from R2.

name: CC6.3 The entity authorizes, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other protected informati
description:
CC6.3 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity authorizes, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other protected information assets based on roles and responsibilities.

Grant people only the minimum access they need to do their jobs, and separate conflicting duties so no single person can commit fraud undetected. Document what access each role should have, require approval for access changes, regularly review whether access is still appropriate, and ensure incompatible functions (like requesting and approving payments) are separated.

Implementation: PropelAuth roles define application access and IAM roles enforce AWS permissions. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, PropelAuth Roles, PropelAuth Users.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.4.1 Cloud Infrastructure Physical Security Assurance
description:
As a fully remote organization utilizing cloud infrastructure, the entity shall maintain documented assurance that all cloud service providers and data center facilities housing company data implement appropriate physical security controls. This includes obtaining and reviewing SOC 2 reports or equivalent attestations from cloud providers, maintaining an inventory of all third-party facilities where company data resides, and ensuring contractual requirements for physical security are in place. The entity shall verify that providers implement access controls, environmental protections, and visitor management procedures commensurate with the sensitivity of data stored.

Implementation: AWS data centers provide physical access controls, environmental protections, and 24/7 security; the AWS SOC 2 report is reviewed in the compliance platform vendor assessment.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC6.4.2 Remote Employee Equipment and Media Security
description:
The entity shall establish and enforce policies governing the physical security of company-owned equipment and any media containing sensitive information at remote work locations. Personnel shall be required to implement reasonable physical safeguards for laptops, mobile devices, and any physical media containing company data. This includes secure storage when not in use, prohibition of leaving devices unattended in public spaces, and proper handling and destruction of any physical documents or media containing sensitive information. The policy shall address equipment return procedures upon termination and reporting requirements for lost or stolen devices.

Implementation: Devices are encrypted with FileVault and stored securely; lost or stolen devices are reported within 24 hours under the Information Security Policy. Evidence: MacOS FileVault Status.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: confirm; 24-hour reporting kept from v1; the Acceptable Use Policy v2 says "immediately" (CONFIRM).

name: CC6.4 The entity restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets.
description:
CC6.4 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets.

Control who can physically access your servers, network equipment, backup media, and paper records containing sensitive information. Use locks, badges, or keys to restrict access, maintain logs of who enters secure areas, escort visitors, and promptly revoke physical access when no longer needed. Even small offices need basic physical security for IT equipment.

Implementation: The organization is fully remote; physical security is provided by AWS SOC 2 attested data centers.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.5.1 Data Sanitization and Media Destruction Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal procedures for the secure sanitization and destruction of data storage media prior to disposal, reuse, or transfer. Given the remote work environment, these procedures must address both company-owned and employee-owned devices that may contain company data. Procedures shall specify approved methods for data wiping (using industry-standard tools meeting NIST 800-88 guidelines) and physical destruction requirements for media that cannot be adequately sanitized. The procedures must also address the secure disposal of paper documents containing sensitive information through shredding or secure destruction services.

Implementation: Cloud data is disposed of by S3 lifecycle deletion and KMS cryptographic erasure; device media are wiped to NIST 800-88 under the Data Retention and Disposal Policy. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.5.2 Asset Disposal Verification and Documentation
description:
The organization shall implement a verification process to confirm that all sensitive information has been removed from assets before discontinuing logical and physical protections. This includes maintaining an inventory of assets pending disposal, documenting the chain of custody during the disposal process, and retaining destruction records for audit purposes. For the remote workforce, this process must include procedures for personnel to return or certify the sanitization of company data from devices used for work purposes, including laptops, mobile devices, and removable storage media.

Implementation: KMS key deletion is logged in CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs and S3 access logs evidence deletion; a dated disposal entry is recorded in the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, AWS KMS Keys.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific.

name: CC6.5 The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive i
description:
CC6.5 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive information from the assets.

Before disposing of computers, drives, phones, or paper documents, ensure data cannot be recovered by others. Wipe or physically destroy storage media, shred sensitive documents, and remove company data from employee devices before reuse or disposal. Keep records of destruction for sensitive data to prove proper disposal.

Implementation: KMS cryptographic erasure, S3 lifecycle rules, and the scheduled retention-enforcement Lambda dispose of data at the triggers set in the Data Retention and Disposal Policy. Evidence: AWS KMS Keys, AWS Lambda Functions.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC6.6.1 Network Perimeter Security Controls
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain network perimeter security controls to protect against external threats. Given the remote work environment, this includes cloud-based firewall solutions, secure DNS filtering, and network segmentation for any cloud infrastructure. All external-facing services must be protected by appropriate security controls, with unnecessary ports and services disabled. Security configurations shall be documented and reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with current threat landscape.

Implementation: Infrastructure sits in private VPC subnets behind security groups; public entry is CloudFront with AWS Shield Standard and TLS 1.2+, with origin access restricted to the Lambda function URLs. Evidence: AWS Security Groups.
notes: Implementation: r4; Perimeter wording from the R4 WAF row.

name: CC6.6.2 Secure Remote Access Management
description:
The organization shall establish secure remote access mechanisms for all personnel accessing company systems. Given the fully cloud-based architecture, the organization implements a zero-trust approach where all access requires authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, regardless of network location. Access is granted based on the principle of least privilege through IAM roles, and all access sessions are logged via CloudTrail and application audit logs. This approach provides equivalent or better security than traditional VPN for a cloud-native organization.

Implementation: Company systems are reached only through browser SSO (Google Workspace) and the AWS console/CLI with MFA; no VPN is used, IAM enforces least privilege, and CloudTrail and CloudWatch log all access. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, PropelAuth Mfa Settings, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Implementation: r4, r5; "PropelAuth + MFA" -> R4/R5 remote-access wording.

name: CC6.6.3 Threat Detection and Security Monitoring
description:
The organization shall deploy and maintain threat detection capabilities to identify and respond to external threats. This includes intrusion detection or prevention systems, security monitoring tools, and alerting mechanisms for suspicious activities. Security tools shall be configured to detect current threat patterns and updated regularly to address emerging threats. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and significant security events shall be escalated according to established procedures.

Implementation: Security-relevant CloudTrail events trigger an EventBridge rule to the breach-detection Lambda, which alerts the CEO via SNS in real time; CloudWatch alarms and VPC Flow Logs provide alerting. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS Security Groups, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: r4; Detection mechanism from the R4 GuardDuty row. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC6.6 The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its sys
description:
CC6.6 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.

Protect your network perimeter from external threats using firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and secure remote access methods like VPNs. Monitor and restrict what can connect to your network from the internet, require extra authentication for external access, and keep security tools updated to detect new threats.

Implementation: Security groups restrict traffic, network ACLs add a second layer, and DocumentDB is not reachable from the internet. Evidence: AWS Security Groups, AWS VPC Subnets.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.7.1 Data Transmission Encryption Standards
description:
The organization shall implement and enforce encryption standards for all sensitive data transmitted across networks. This includes mandatory TLS 1.2 or higher for web communications, encrypted email protocols, and secure API connections. All remote work communications must traverse encrypted channels, and VPN or zero-trust network access shall be required for accessing internal systems from external locations.

Implementation: All endpoints are HTTPS only with TLS 1.2+ and ACM-managed certificates; API keys are managed in PropelAuth. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, PropelAuth Api Keys.
notes: Implementation: r4; ACM/TLS per R4.

name: CC6.7.2 Removable Media and Data Transfer Controls
description:
The organization shall establish formal controls governing external data transfers. Given the fully remote, cloud-first work environment where company data resides entirely in cloud services (AWS, PropelAuth), controls focus on securing cloud access rather than removable media. Approved secure methods shall be designated for sensitive document exchange, with appropriate access controls enforced via IAM and PropelAuth roles.

Implementation: All data lives in AWS (DocumentDB, S3) and is reached only through PropelAuth and IAM; TLS 1.2+ protects data in transit. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, AWS S3 Bucket Encryption, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.7.3 Mobile Device Data Protection
description:
The organization shall implement controls to protect company data accessed from remote devices. This includes mandatory device encryption (FileVault for macOS), strong authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, and session management controls. Centralized mobile device management (MDM) is not required; instead, security is enforced through encryption, authentication, and access controls at the application layer.

Implementation: FileVault encrypts all macOS devices, customer sign-in is Google SSO through PropelAuth with session timeout configured, and lost devices are reported within 24 hours under the Information Security Policy. Evidence: MacOS FileVault Status, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5, confirm; MFA wording per R5; 24-hour reporting CONFIRM (see CC6.4.2).

name: CC6.7.4 Unauthorized Data Transfer Monitoring
description:
The organization shall implement monitoring mechanisms to detect and alert on unauthorized data transfers or anomalous data movement patterns. This includes monitoring of cloud application usage, large file transfers, and access to sensitive data repositories. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and suspected unauthorized transfers shall be investigated and documented.

Implementation: DocumentDB requires TLS, and CloudWatch Logs, CloudTrail, and VPC Flow Logs record data access for review. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, AWS DocumentDB Cluster, CloudTrail Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.7 The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and externa
description:
CC6.7 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and external users and processes.

Control and protect data when it moves outside your direct control. Use encryption for sensitive data in transit, restrict the use of removable media like USB drives, implement secure file sharing instead of email for sensitive documents, and protect mobile devices that access company data. Monitor for unauthorized data transfers.

Implementation: TLS 1.2+ protects all data in transit, endpoints are HTTPS only, and access requires PropelAuth or IAM authentication. Evidence: AWS IAM Roles, PropelAuth Security Settings.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC6.8.1 Endpoint Protection and Antivirus Management
description:
The organization shall maintain endpoint protection capabilities across company-managed devices. For macOS devices, this includes reliance on built-in macOS security features (XProtect, Gatekeeper, MRT) supplemented by cloud-based scanning of code and containers. Endpoint protection focuses on secure device configuration, encryption, and cloud-native security tools rather than traditional enterprise endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.

Implementation: FileVault full-disk encryption, XProtect, and Gatekeeper protect personnel macOS devices; ECR scan-on-push, Dependabot and code scanning, and Trivy in CI cover containers and code. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, AWS ECR Repositories, Configuration-check record (monthly), MacOS FileVault Status.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r4; R4 device-agent wording superseded by D4 (FileVault only). Decisions applied: D4, D12.

name: CC6.8.2 Software Installation Controls and Patch Management
description:
The organization shall establish controls governing software installation and maintain current patch levels across all systems. Administrative privileges for software installation shall be restricted to authorized personnel only. A documented process shall exist for evaluating, approving, and deploying software updates and security patches in a timely manner. For the remote workforce, this includes ensuring personal devices used for work purposes comply with minimum security requirements.

Implementation: Dependabot proposes dependency updates that merge through the pull-request CI gate; critical dependency CVEs are remediated within 7 days. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, GitHub Secret Scanning.
notes: Implementation: r5; Remediation SLA per R5.

name: CC6.8.3 Security Awareness and Malware Response Procedures
description:
The organization shall provide security awareness training to all personnel covering recognition of phishing attempts, social engineering tactics, and safe handling of files from external sources. A documented incident response procedure shall exist for malware detection events, including immediate containment steps, notification requirements, and remediation actions. Cross-training shall ensure that more than one person can execute response procedures.

Implementation: Security-awareness training covers phishing and malware, and the Incident Response Procedure defines containment steps for malware events. Evidence: Ethics And Security Training Completion Certificate Mo Messidi.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC6.8 The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorized or malicious
description:
CC6.8 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorized or malicious software.

Protect against viruses, malware, and unauthorized software installations. Deploy and maintain antivirus software, restrict who can install programs, keep all software patched and updated, scan files from external sources, and train users to recognize phishing and other attacks. Have a process to respond quickly when malware is detected.

Implementation: ECR scan-on-push scans containers, Dependabot and code scanning cover dependencies (21 alerts tracked), and Trivy runs in CI. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, AWS ECR Repositories, Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Implementation: r4, confirm; v1 "Code scanning via AWS not GitHub" conflicts with the R4 table (GitHub code scanning); CONFIRM. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.1.1 Security Configuration Baseline and Change Monitoring
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented security configuration baselines for all critical systems, infrastructure components, and applications. Automated monitoring mechanisms shall be implemented to detect unauthorized or unplanned configuration changes that may introduce security vulnerabilities. Cloud-native configuration management and monitoring tools shall be utilized to ensure continuous oversight without requiring dedicated on-premises infrastructure.

Implementation: CloudFormation (serverless deploy) is the only change path and reports drift; the monthly configuration-check Lambda (CloudTrail, S3 public access, security groups, root MFA, IAM password policy, KMS rotation, ECR scan-on-push, DocumentDB backups) and the CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule detect unplanned changes. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), CloudTrail Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r4; Baseline/drift wording from the R4 AWS Config row. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.1.2 Vulnerability Scanning and Assessment Program
description:
The organization shall implement a formal vulnerability scanning and assessment program to identify security weaknesses across all systems, applications, and infrastructure components. Regular automated vulnerability scans shall be conducted at defined intervals, with results documented, analyzed, and prioritized based on risk severity. The program shall include subscription to relevant threat intelligence feeds and security advisories pertinent to the organization's technology stack to ensure timely awareness of newly discovered vulnerabilities.

Implementation: Dependabot, code scanning, ECR scan-on-push, and Trivy in CI scan continuously; the configuration-check Lambda posts a monthly pass/fail record that is reviewed monthly, and security-relevant CloudTrail events alert in real time. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, Configuration-check record (monthly).
notes: Implementation: r5; Monthly review per R5. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.1 The entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in t
description:
CC7.1 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in the introduction of new vulnerabilities, and (2) susceptibilities to newly discovered vulnerabilities.

Continuously watch for new security weaknesses in your systems. Use standard security configurations, regularly scan for vulnerabilities, monitor for unauthorized system changes, and stay informed about new threats affecting your technology. When vulnerabilities are found, assess their risk and fix them based on severity.

Implementation: ECR scan-on-push, Dependabot, code scanning, and Trivy in CI detect new vulnerabilities; the monthly configuration-check Lambda and the CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule detect configuration changes. Evidence: GitHub Dependabot, AWS ECR Repositories, Configuration-check record (monthly), CloudTrail Events.
notes: Implementation: r4, confirm; GuardDuty removed; code-scanning location CONFIRM (see CC6.8). Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.2.1 Security Monitoring Infrastructure Implementation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a centralized security monitoring infrastructure. This includes deployment of cloud-native monitoring solutions capable of aggregating logs and security events from all critical systems, including cloud infrastructure, SaaS applications, endpoints, and identity providers. Given the remote work environment, particular emphasis shall be placed on monitoring authentication systems, VPN connections, and cloud service access patterns. The monitoring infrastructure shall be configured to provide real-time visibility into system health and security posture.

Implementation: CloudTrail logs all AWS API calls with integrity validation, CloudWatch Logs retain application and VPC Flow Logs for 90 days, and the configuration-check Lambda posts a monthly pass/fail record to the compliance platform. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.2.2 Anomaly Detection and Alerting Configuration
description:
The organization shall configure automated detection rules and alerting mechanisms to identify anomalies indicative of security incidents, system failures, or operational issues. Detection rules shall address authentication anomalies (failed login attempts, impossible travel scenarios, unusual access times), unauthorized configuration changes, unexpected file modifications to critical systems, abnormal network traffic patterns, and system performance degradation. Alerts shall be prioritized by severity and routed to appropriate personnel through established communication channels suitable for a remote workforce, ensuring timely response regardless of location.

Implementation: CloudWatch alarms fire on API errors and latency (p95 > 2 seconds) and on Lambda failures; security-relevant CloudTrail events are routed through EventBridge and the breach-detection Lambda to SNS in real time. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, Lambda App Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; Thresholds per R5/R4. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.2.3 Monitoring Review and Response Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for the regular review of monitoring data and timely response to detected anomalies. Procedures shall define clear ownership for monitoring review responsibilities, establish minimum review frequencies appropriate for the organization's risk profile, and document escalation procedures for identified anomalies. The procedures shall include guidance for initial triage, investigation steps, and criteria for escalating to incident response processes. Regular review of monitoring effectiveness shall be conducted to ensure continued alignment with organizational objectives.

Implementation: The CEO reviews the configuration-check record monthly and receives SNS security-event alerts in real time; logs are retained 90 days and the Incident Response Procedure sets triage and escalation. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events, Lambda App Events.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.2 The entity monitors system components and the operation of controls to detect anomalies that are indicative of
description:
CC7.2 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity monitors system components and the operation of controls to detect anomalies that are indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors affecting the entity's ability to meet its objectives.

Set up monitoring to detect unusual activities that might indicate an attack or system problem. This includes watching for strange login patterns, unexpected file changes, unusual network traffic, or system performance issues. Use automated tools where possible and ensure alerts reach the right people quickly.

Implementation: CloudTrail logs every API call with integrity validation and is retained 7 years; CloudWatch alarms and Logs (90 days) cover application events. Evidence: GitHub Actions Workflows, AWS CloudWatch Alarms, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events, Lambda App Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: r5; CloudTrail 90-day retention -> 7 years (R5).

name: CC7.3.1 Security Event Triage and Classification Procedure
description:
The organization shall maintain a documented procedure for triaging and classifying security events to determine whether they constitute security incidents requiring escalation. This procedure shall define clear criteria for distinguishing between routine events, anomalies, and confirmed security incidents. The procedure shall include defined severity levels, classification criteria, and designated personnel responsible for initial triage decisions. The procedure shall be accessible to all personnel and reviewed annually.

Implementation: The Incident Response Procedure defines severity levels P1 to P4, classification criteria, and the CEO as triage owner; alerts arrive via SNS. Evidence: AWS SNS Topics.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific; Severity scale per Q2.

name: CC7.3.2 Security Event Investigation and Escalation Process
description:
The organization shall implement a formal process for investigating security events and escalating confirmed incidents. This process shall include defined investigation steps, impact assessment criteria, escalation thresholds, and communication protocols appropriate for a distributed remote team. The process shall specify timeframes for initial assessment, define escalation paths, and document how lessons learned from investigated events are captured and used to improve detection and prevention capabilities.

Implementation: CloudWatch alarms publish to SNS topics; P1 events are acknowledged within 4 business hours and investigated under the Incident Response Procedure. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, CloudTrail Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: r4; Response target per R4.

name: CC7.3 The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they are security incidents.
description:
CC7.3 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they are security incidents.

When security alerts occur, quickly determine if they represent real threats that could harm your operations or compromise data. Have a process to investigate events, assess their potential impact, and escalate true incidents for immediate response. Learn from events to improve detection and prevention.

Implementation: Security-event SNS alerts and failed configuration-check items are evaluated against CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs; the compliance platform incident register shows 0 open incidents and 100 % SLA compliance. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Alarms, Configuration-check record (monthly), AWS SNS Topics, CloudTrail Events, Compliance Platform Incident Reporting, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: humadroid. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.4.1 Incident Response Program Documentation
description:
Establish and maintain a formal incident response program that defines the organization's approach to handling security incidents. The program shall include clear definitions of what constitutes a security incident, severity classification criteria, escalation thresholds, and response timeframes appropriate to each severity level. The program should be streamlined yet comprehensive, with clear decision trees that enable rapid response without bureaucratic delays. The documentation must be readily accessible to all personnel and reviewed annually or following significant incidents.

Implementation: The Incident Response Procedure defines incident criteria, severity levels P1 to P4, escalation thresholds, and response targets, and is reviewed annually.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: specific.

name: CC7.4.2 Incident Response Roles and Responsibilities
description:
Define and assign incident response roles and responsibilities across the organization, accounting for the remote work environment. Designate primary and backup incident commanders, establish clear communication chains, and document criteria for engaging external resources such as legal counsel, forensic specialists, or law enforcement. Ensure all personnel understand their specific responsibilities during an incident and maintain current contact information for all internal and external parties who may need to be engaged during incident response.

Implementation: The CEO is incident commander; the Incident Response Procedure documents roles, the escalation chain, and criteria for engaging external parties. Evidence: Organizational Structure.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: confirm; Requirement asks for a backup incident commander; none is named (CONFIRM).

name: CC7.4.3 Incident Containment, Mitigation, and Remediation Procedures
description:
Establish documented procedures for containing, mitigating, and remediating security incidents. Containment procedures shall address immediate actions to prevent incident spread, including network isolation protocols, account suspension processes, and system quarantine methods appropriate for a remote work environment. Mitigation procedures shall outline steps to reduce ongoing impact while permanent solutions are developed. Remediation procedures shall detail the process for eliminating root causes, closing vulnerabilities, removing unauthorized access, and safely restoring systems to normal operations with verification that threats have been fully eliminated.

Implementation: Containment uses IAM credential revocation and VPC isolation; remediation and recovery steps are in the Incident Response Procedure. Evidence: AWS SNS Topics, CloudTrail Events, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: none.

name: CC7.4.4 Incident Documentation and Communication Protocols
description:
Implement standardized incident documentation and communication protocols to ensure thorough recording of all incident response activities and timely notification to relevant stakeholders. Documentation requirements shall include incident timeline, actions taken, personnel involved, evidence preserved, and lessons learned. Communication protocols shall define notification requirements and timeframes for internal management, affected customers, and regulatory bodies as applicable. Establish templates and channels appropriate for remote team coordination during active incidents.

Implementation: Incidents are documented on the Incident Response Procedure template with evidence from CloudWatch Logs and CloudTrail retained 7 years; notifications go out via SNS and customers are notified within 48 hours. Evidence: AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, AWS SNS Topics, CloudTrail Events.
notes: Implementation: r5; Evidence retention and notification window per R5.

name: CC7.4.5 Post-Incident Review and Program Improvement
description:
Conduct post-incident reviews following all significant security incidents to evaluate response effectiveness and identify improvement opportunities. Reviews shall analyze incident handling performance against established procedures, identify gaps or inefficiencies, and generate actionable recommendations. Maintain records of lessons learned and track implementation of improvements to the incident response program. Periodically analyze incident patterns to identify systemic issues requiring attention beyond individual incident remediation.

Implementation: Post-incident reviews follow the Incident Response Procedure and lessons learned are minuted in the quarterly management meeting. Evidence: Board Management Meeting Minutes Q4 2025.
notes: Implementation: role; Board -> management.

name: CC7.4 The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident response program.
description:
CC7.4 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident response program.

Establish a comprehensive incident response program that activates when security incidents occur. Clearly assign roles and responsibilities - everyone should know their part when an incident strikes, including when to bring in external help. First, work to understand the nature and severity of the incident to determine the right response strategy and timeframe. Implement containment procedures to stop active threats from spreading or causing more damage. Deploy mitigation techniques to reduce ongoing impact while you work on permanent fixes. Execute remediation to close vulnerabilities and remove unauthorized access. Restore normal operations safely, ensuring threats are fully eliminated before bringing systems back online. Develop communication protocols for timely updates to affected parties, management, customers, and regulators as required. Document all actions taken during incident response. Periodically evaluate your response effectiveness and update procedures based on lessons learned. Review incident patterns to identify systemic issues needing attention. The goal is coordinated, effective response that minimizes damage and prevents recurrence.

Implementation: The Incident Response Procedure defines roles, escalation, containment, and remediation; the compliance platform incident register shows 0 open incidents and 100 % SLA compliance, and the CloudTrail-EventBridge security-event rule and the monthly configuration-check Lambda provide detection. Evidence: Configuration-check record (monthly), AWS SNS Topics, CloudTrail Events, Compliance Platform Incident Reporting, VPC Flow Events.
notes: Implementation: humadroid. Decisions applied: D12.

name: CC7.5.1 Security Incident Recovery Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented procedures for recovering from identified security incidents. These procedures shall address system restoration priorities, data recovery from backups, verification of system integrity prior to returning to production, and implementation of additional controls to prevent incident recurrence. Given the remote work environment, procedures shall include specific guidance for recovering both cloud-based infrastructure and remote endpoint systems.

Implementation: The Business Continuity Plan documents recovery from security incidents, with DocumentDB point-in-time recovery and CloudFormation redeploy as the recovery path. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails.
notes: Implementation: specific.

name: CC7.5.2 Recovery Procedure Testing and Validation
description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing of incident recovery procedures to validate their effectiveness and ensure operational readiness. Testing shall occur at least annually and following significant changes to systems or infrastructure. Test results shall be documented, including any identified gaps or improvements, and procedures shall be updated accordingly. Tabletop exercises and targeted recovery drills are acceptable testing methods.

Implementation: The BCP full test of February 4, 2026 exercised incident recovery (full system recovery from backups using infrastructure as code); backup restores are tested quarterly and the BCP annually. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; Quarterly restore test per R3/R5; "Q1 2025" label dropped (D18).

name: CC7.5 The entity identifies, develops, and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.
description:
CC7.5 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity identifies, develops, and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.

Plan how to restore operations after a security incident. This includes rebuilding compromised systems, restoring data from backups, implementing additional controls to prevent recurrence, and verifying that systems are clean before returning to production. Test your recovery procedures regularly to ensure they work when needed.

Implementation: Recovery follows the Business Continuity Plan: restore DocumentDB from backups or point-in-time recovery and redeploy with CloudFormation; CloudWatch and CloudTrail verify the restored system. Evidence: AWS CloudTrail Trails, AWS CloudWatch Log Groups, CloudTrail Events, Lambda App Events.
notes: Implementation: r4; GuardDuty removed; v1 note did not describe recovery.

name: CC8.1.1 Change Management Authorization and Documentation
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal change management process requiring documented authorization before any system changes commence. All changes must be logged with appropriate details including requestor, approver, risk assessment, and business justification. The CEO must approve changes based on documented risk and impact assessment. Emergency change procedures shall be established for critical fixes while maintaining appropriate controls and retrospective documentation.

Implementation: Every change is a pull request on the protected main branch approved by the CEO after CI passes; emergency changes use a PR labelled emergency with post-hoc review within 5 business days, and deployment is by CloudFormation. Evidence: GitHub Deploy Workflow, AWS Cloudformation Stacks.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; Authorization and emergency path per R3/R5.

name: CC8.1.2 Secure Development and Testing Practices
description:
The organization shall implement secure development practices ensuring security requirements are considered from the design phase. All changes must undergo appropriate testing before production deployment, including functional testing and security review proportionate to the change scope. Testing responsibilities shall be clearly defined with documented results. Secure baseline configurations shall be established and maintained for all system components, with monitoring for unauthorized deviations.

Implementation: Pull requests must pass CI status checks (lint, tests, Bandit, Trivy, TruffleHog) and are validated on the staging stage before merge to main. Evidence: GitHub Branch Protection.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; "PR approval" -> CI gate + staging (R3).

name: CC8.1.3 Controlled Deployment and Segregation of Duties
description:
The organization shall implement controlled deployment procedures ensuring changes are moved to production in a systematic manner. Appropriate segregation of duties shall be maintained where feasible; at minimum, every production deployment shall pass through a pull request on the protected main branch with required CI status checks and a logged self-review before merge. Final stakeholder approval must be obtained before implementation, with documented acceptance of any residual risks. Patch management procedures shall ensure security updates are evaluated, tested, and deployed promptly based on criticality assessment.

Implementation: Production deploys only from a green CI run on a pull request with a logged self-review, merged by the CEO as final approver; Dependabot updates follow the same path. Evidence: GitHub Branch Protection.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; Segregation replaced by the R2 compensating control.

name: CC8.1 The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains system com
description:
CC8.1 (CC8 - Change Management): The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains system components that are consistent with defined system security and availability objectives.

Implement a comprehensive change management process covering the entire system lifecycle. Require proper authorization before any changes begin - someone with appropriate authority must approve based on risk and impact. Design and develop changes securely, considering security requirements from the start. Document all changes thoroughly so others can understand and maintain them. Track changes through the entire process to prevent unauthorized modifications from slipping through. Configure software using secure baselines and monitor for deviations. Test all changes before production deployment - including unit testing, integration testing, security testing, and user acceptance testing. Obtain final approval before implementation, ensuring stakeholders understand and accept any risks. Deploy changes in a controlled manner with proper segregation of duties - developers shouldn't push their own code to production. Identify which objectives are affected by each change and verify the system still meets them. Include changes needed to remediate security incidents in your process. Maintain baseline configurations of all systems. Have emergency change procedures for critical fixes that still maintain appropriate controls. Manage patches systematically - evaluate, test, and deploy security updates promptly based on criticality.

Implementation: GitHub branch protection requires a pull request with passing CI status checks before merge, and CloudFormation deploys the same stack to staging and production. Evidence: GitHub Deploy Workflow, GitHub Workflow Run Details, GitHub Branch Protection.
notes: Implementation: r5; "PR review required" -> PR + CI gate.

name: CC9.1.1 Business Impact Analysis and Critical Asset Identification
description:
The organization shall conduct and maintain a formal business impact analysis to identify critical systems, applications, and data essential to business operations. This analysis must document recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for each critical asset, prioritize systems based on business criticality, and identify dependencies between systems. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to cloud-based systems, collaboration tools, and remote access infrastructure that enable distributed operations.

Implementation: The Business Continuity Plan identifies critical systems with RTO/RPO; the compliance platform BCP dashboard records AWS infrastructure (RTO 2 hours), customer data pipeline (RTO 4 hours), and DocumentDB (RTO 4 hours). Evidence: Compliance Platform Bcp Dashboard.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, confirm; "MongoDB" -> DocumentDB (Q2); CONFIRM the dashboard label.

name: CC9.1.2 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Planning
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans that address potential disruptions including cybersecurity incidents, natural disasters, and service provider outages. Plans must include data backup and recovery procedures, alternate work arrangements suitable for the existing remote workforce, communication protocols for team coordination during incidents, and defined roles and responsibilities. Plans shall be reviewed annually and updated when significant business changes occur.

Implementation: DocumentDB runs a single serverless instance with storage replicated across three availability zones, automatic re-creation of the instance after any failure, including an availability-zone failure, in a single region (us-east-1) by design; the compliance platform BCP dashboard shows 8 active plans with 0 overdue exercises. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Cluster, Compliance Platform Bcp Dashboard.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, r4; "geographic redundancy" -> single region per R4.

name: CC9.1.3 Continuity Plan Testing and Validation
description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing of business continuity and disaster recovery plans to validate their effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. Testing activities shall include backup restoration verification, recovery procedure walkthroughs, and communication protocol exercises. Test results must be documented, and identified deficiencies shall be remediated in a timely manner. Tabletop exercises and targeted recovery tests are acceptable testing methods.

Implementation: The BCP full test executed February 4, 2026 (full system recovery from backups using infrastructure as code) completed with a 100 % success rate; backup restores are tested quarterly. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, Compliance Platform Bcp Test Results.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: r5; "Q1 2025" label dropped (D18).

name: CC9.1 The entity identifies, selects, and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential busin
description:
CC9.1 (CC9 - Risk Mitigation): The entity identifies, selects, and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential business disruptions.

Plan for events that could disrupt your business operations - from ransomware attacks to natural disasters. Identify critical systems and data, develop backup and recovery procedures, establish alternate work arrangements, and consider insurance coverage. Test your continuity plans regularly and update them as your business changes.

Implementation: The Business Continuity Plan sets RTO/RPO; the compliance platform BCP dashboard holds 8 processes (7 critical) and 8 active plans, backed by DocumentDB storage replicated across three availability zones with 35-day point-in-time recovery. Evidence: AWS DocumentDB Backups, AWS DocumentDB Cluster, Compliance Platform Bcp Dashboard.
notes: Implementation: humadroid.

name: CC9.2.1 Vendor Risk Assessment and Due Diligence
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for evaluating the security posture of vendors and business partners prior to engagement. This includes conducting security assessments proportionate to the risk level of the services provided, reviewing vendor security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001), evaluating their data handling practices, and documenting risk acceptance decisions. This process should be streamlined yet thorough, focusing on vendors with access to sensitive data or critical systems.

Implementation: Vendors are assessed in the compliance platform before engagement; the AWS assessment verifies SOC 2 Type II and assigns risk tier Critical. Evidence: Compliance Platform Vendor Assessment.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC9.2.2 Vendor Contractual Security Requirements
description:
The organization shall ensure that all vendor and business partner agreements include appropriate security requirements, data protection obligations, and compliance provisions. Contracts must address confidentiality obligations, data handling and return/destruction requirements, security incident notification procedures, right to audit provisions, and termination procedures. Standard security addendum templates should be developed for efficient contract management.

Implementation: The Privacy Notice and Data Processing Agreement Template sets confidentiality, breach notification, audit rights, and termination terms for vendor agreements.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: none.

name: CC9.2.3 Ongoing Vendor Monitoring and Contingency Planning
description:
The organization shall implement procedures for ongoing monitoring of vendor compliance with security requirements and maintain contingency plans for critical vendor relationships. This includes periodic reassessment of vendor security posture, monitoring for vendor security incidents or breaches, and documenting alternative arrangements for critical services. Annual reviews of critical vendors and documented backup options for essential services are appropriate.

Implementation: Critical vendors are reassessed annually in the compliance platform vendor dashboard (AWS and PropelAuth most recently), and the Business Continuity Plan documents vendor contingency. Evidence: Compliance Platform Vendor Dashboard.
notes: Requirement: R2 edit(s). Implementation: humadroid, r5; "2 months ago" relative date removed; annual cadence per R5.

name: CC9.2 The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.
description:
CC9.2 (CC9 - Risk Mitigation): The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.

Understand and manage the security risks from third parties who have access to your systems or data. Evaluate vendor security before engagement, include security requirements in contracts, monitor vendor compliance, and have contingency plans if a vendor fails. Pay special attention to vendors handling sensitive data or providing critical services.

Implementation: The compliance platform vendor register tracks 5 vendors with risk tiers and assessment status: AWS and PropelAuth as sub-processors, and GitHub, Google Workspace, and Resend as vendors that do not process customer data. Evidence: Compliance Platform Vendor Dashboard.
notes: Implementation: humadroid, r5; Vendor count 2 -> 5. Decisions applied: D15.
